title: Runbook Recommendation Agent — telemetry-driven admin assistant
creator: Nora Patel
description: Build a lightweight recommendation agent that surfaces candidate runbook steps (or shortflow playlets) for on-call/support engineers based on recent telemetry, alert context, and historical runbook outcomes. The agent should be read-only by default (suggestions only), and able to produce: ranked step fragments, relevant prior incidents, and confidence signals. Goal is to accelerate triage and reduce MTTR for frequent classes of incidents while maintaining strict auditability and safety guards.
acceptance_criteria: Agent integrated into the ops console suggestion pane and visible on alert pages
Suggestions include at least: top-3 runbook fragments, links to prior incidents (last 90d), and a confidence score
Read-only suggestion flow implemented and no automatic execution in the initial launch
Backend can score suggestions within 250ms P95 for a typical alert payload
Telemetry events emitted for suggestion shown/clicked and suggestion feedback (useful/not useful)
Include an admin toggle to disable suggestions per-team via Console feature flags
technical_notes: Input signals: alert metadata (service, severity, tags), recent APM traces, error group fingerprints, and runbook execution logs
Scoring model: simple heuristic + retrieval-augmented ranking using cosine similarity over runbook embeddings; baseline uses precomputed fragment embeddings updated nightly
Storage: fragment index lives in dedicated vector store cluster (V2 shard) scoped to prod region
Privacy: redact any customer-identifying fields from telemetry before embedding/lookup
Safety: suggestions include provenance (runbook id + snippet id + last-run result) and confidence thresholds to suppress low-quality matches
Latency optimizations: prefix KV cache for hot services, async warmup for known noisy alerts, batched vector queries when evaluating multiple alerts
Fallback: if vector store unavailable, surface a generic troubleshooting checklist cached in the service fallback layer
plan: Week 1: spike — prototype retrieval pipeline using existing fragment corpus and compute embeddings (local) (owner: Diego)
Week 2: implement suggestion API (read-only), UI mockups in Console (owner: Design/Elena), establish telemetry event schema
Week 3: integrate vector store, nightly embedding updater, and safety filter service; run offline evaluation on past incidents
Week 4: closed beta with two support squads, collect feedback and label usefulness signals
Week 5: harden performance, add team-level feature flag, and prepare rollout playbook
rollout_steps: Deploy backend service to canary region with feature flag off
Enable for two internal support squads and observe suggestion metrics for 72 hours
Collect feedback, iterate on ranking weights, and harden redaction rules
Enable read-only suggestions for all internal support teams
After 2 weeks of stable telemetry and <5% false-positive feedback, evaluate affordance for safe, opt-in action execution (separate project)
risks: Low-quality suggestions could increase cognitive load and harm trust — mitigate with conservative thresholds and enforced provenance
Embedding drift: nightly updates might surface different fragments over time — rollbacks and deterministic seeding required
Latency regressions on alert pages if vector queries are not optimized — add caching and early-bail heuristics
Data privacy: sensitive fields in traces must be removed before embedding — add redaction pipeline and review with Security
Operational: vector store OOM or downtime could degrade suggestion availability — provide fallback checklist
metrics: Impact on MTTR for enabled squads (goal: 10% reduction over baseline after 4 weeks)
False-positive suggestion rate (manual review sample target <5%)
